exposure: latency after preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM)
Latency after preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM)
Gestational age at PPROM (32(+0)-33(+6) weeks and 34(+0)-36(+6) weeks)
cohort: Singleton pregnancies with non-malformed fetuses in cephalic presentation complicated by PPROM at 32(+0)-36(+6) weeks
finding: In moderately to late PPROM, increased latency is associated with higher risk of EONI and cesarean section with no reduction in RDS.
mod_finding: Increased latency after PPROM is associated with a higher rate of cesarean section.
